chapter: Suntaug Lake Inn and Duke Ellington's band
title: 'A million dollars worth of diamonds' at the Vancouver border
summary: Whaley jokes to a customs officer, who has the bus unloaded, and he is nicknamed 'million dollars worth of diamonds Whaley'.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: I'll tell you another thing about, we was up there in British Columbia, you know where that is.
Way up in the northeast -- west part of the United States there, up there above Washington State. And we would -- we were doing a gig up there in what's the name of the town.
I can't tell you the town. There was a club up there that all the bands used to play there. Triangle Club or something like that.
And we got up there late, see, and we

didn't have time to eat or anything, sat up the band and go on to work and we got through, the band boy put the things on the bus and we were all waiting. We got down to the port of embarkation and we were all waiting around there so I'm about 20 feet from the bus, I'm by myself, because I'm waiting in a hurry to get back into town where I can get something to eat.

So one of these officers come up to me and says and what did you buy. I says what I did. He says, 'what did you buy.' I said, 'you know we didn't have time to eat anything. "Oh, what did I buy. I bought a million dollars worth of diamonds!" His face turned red, he turned around, take everything off that bus. Duke comes over and says, 'what did you tell the man?' I said the man asked me what did I buy and I told him I bought a million dollars worth of diamonds. I ain't had time to get a drink of water hardly and he asked me that.
So everybody laughed, million dollars worth of diamonds Whaley.
That's right, up there in Vancouver. Beautiful place.
Between the two of us, we can remember almost anything, Tom.
I remember that and everybody, even Steven James, he was there I think --
No, Steven James, Ruth's son. He always remembered that.
